Closes #2212

## What changed and why

The B15/MN09 long-face premise (every catalog face over 260 printed characters prints a short form) moved from the daily-only Cypress component specs into the per-PR web unit tests.

- [shortText.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2212/apps/web/src/cards/shortText.ts) gains the one shared pinned list `LONG_FACES` (28 `"defId base|radiant"` entries, with an `R1017000` comment), beside `SHORT_FORMS`.
- [index.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2212/apps/web/src/cards/index.ts) re-exports `LONG_FACES`.
- [textLimit.test.ts](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2212/apps/web/src/cards/textLimit.test.ts) gains two cases with the same titles the specs used: the B15 premise (computed with `faceModel`, `shortFormOf`, `TEXT_TIER_MAX`; pins `xl` at 260, asserts every long face has a short form, and set-equality with `LONG_FACES`) and the MN09 premise (Meditative set in catalog, Chinese face for every card, longest faces equal the `meditative-` subset, pinning that no Chinese face crosses 260).
- [card-faces.cy.tsx](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2212/e2e/cypress/component/card-faces.cy.tsx) drops its premise test and keeps the 270 px / 170 px pixel tests; the `data-long` diagnostic now also reports `premise-long` membership in `LONG_FACES` (a read with zero pass/fail change; the clamp gate stays `faceText().less`).
- [meditative-faces.cy.tsx](/home/agent-muse/actions-runner/_work/_temp/work/item-2212/e2e/cypress/component/meditative-faces.cy.tsx) drops its premise test; `mayClamp` reads `LONG_FACES` keyed by the underlying face, and the FIT header names the shared list.

No ruling, spec, workflow, or scope-map change: R1017000 already lists `textLimit.test.ts` in `proven_in`, and `scripts/ci-scope.sh` is untouched.

## How it was tested (commands I ran, output I saw)

- Base first: `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/cards/textLimit.test.ts` → 5 passed (the #2067 ordering concern is resolved on this base).
- After the change: same file → 7 passed; `src/net/ci-scope.test.ts` → 124 passed across both files, so no scope-map change is needed.
- Negative proofs by local edits that were restored, never committed: commenting out `SHORT_FORMS["core-093"]` fails the new B15 case with `core-093 base: expected null not to be null`; deleting one `LONG_FACES` entry fails set-equality naming `core-093 base`. `git status --porcelain` afterwards shows only the five intended files.
- `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` green; `pnpm --dir e2e typecheck:component` green; `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` green; neighbouring `fit.test.tsx` + `model.test.ts` → 78 passed; `cargo fmt --check` green.
- `pnpm --dir e2e test:component` could not run here: the Cypress 16.1.0 binary is not installed on this machine (`~/.cache/Cypress` missing). This is the issue's documented fallback, covered by `typecheck:component` plus eslint above.
- `cargo jackioh spec check` reports 1 problem: `spec/rulings/R2102000.md` names Core #2102, which is no card in the catalog. This is pre-existing and unrelated — I reproduced the identical failure on a clean HEAD worktree (removed afterwards) and my diff touches no `spec/` or `crates/` file.

## Decisions the issue did not settle

- Where each deleted premise `it` stood I left a two-line pointer comment to the vitest file, rather than deleting silently. Rejected alternative: no comment (a future reader would wonder where the premise went).
- The B15 unit case reuses the file's existing `DEFS`/`FACES`/`printed()` helper instead of copying the Cypress computation verbatim; the MN09 case mirrors the spec's four face variants exactly, since `faceModel`'s Chinese path has no helper in this file.

```text
# #2212: Patch: the check that every long card face has a short form runs in the web's unit tests on every pull request
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
A card whose text is too long for its frame needs a shorter printed form. The test that checks this runs only in the daily browser run. So a pull request that adds or rewords a long card passes CI and turns the next day's run red. That has happened at least twice, and the night bot then spent a build fixing it. This moves the check, which only reads the card data, into the web's ordinary unit tests, which run on every pull request. The browser test keeps only what needs a real browser, the pixel checks.

## Why
- The premise test, `B15 R1017000 the premise` (`e2e/cypress/component/card-faces.cy.tsx:185-223`), mounts nothing. It works out each face's printed length with `faceModel`, checks that every face over `TEXT_TIER_MAX.xl` (260) has a `shortFormOf`, and pins the list of those faces.
- Component specs run only in the daily super run (its `component` job), or when CI is dispatched with `all` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:39`, `:67`).
- The per-pull-request `apps/web/src/cards/textLimit.test.ts:61-74` checks a line estimate (`FACE_TEXT_LIMIT`), not the 260-character rule. Its header (`:1-4`) leaves that rule to the Cypress spec.
- First slip: `6704528b4` (#974) fixed `component B15` after #967's text for KY's Papaya.
- Second slip: the bot's journal for the open #2067 (`2bf12625d`) records four B15 failures, every one a Stinkyscape face added by #2018. The same journal records a 150-minute build that timed out.

## Proposal
- Move the premise into `apps/web/src/cards/textLimit.test.ts` as a vitest case with the same title, using the same `faceModel`, `shortFormOf` and `TEXT_TIER_MAX`.
- Its pinned list becomes one exported constant that the test and both component specs read. `meditative-faces.cy.tsx:193-216` repeats part of the list.
- The Cypress spec drops its premise test and keeps its pixel tests at 270 px and 170 px.
- Nothing under `.github/` changes, because the web job already runs this file. If `scripts/ci-scope.sh` does not turn the web job on for a card-text-only change, its map gains that path in the same pull request.

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/cards/textLimit.test.ts`, with the pinned list beside `SHORT_FORMS` in `apps/web/src/cards/shortText.ts` or in a fixture under `apps/web/src/cards/`.
- `e2e/cypress/component/card-faces.cy.tsx` and `meditative-faces.cy.tsx`.
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, only if its map lacks a path the moved test reads.
- R1017000 (`spec/rulings/R1017000.md`) already lists `textLimit.test.ts` in `proven_in`, so it needs no new ruling.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/cards/textLimit.test.ts` holds the premise. The PR shows that a face over 260 characters without a short form fails it, and so does a long face missing from the pinned list, each by a local edit that is not committed.
- [ ] Neither component spec keeps a premise test of its own, and all of them read the one shared list.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir e2e test:component` passes `card-faces.cy.tsx` and `meditative-faces.cy.tsx`, or the PR says why it was not run.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` are green.

## Size and risks
Small: about 40 lines across four files.
- Build it after #2067 merges, since #2067 adds the Stinkyscape short forms and updates the list. Until then the moved test is red on `main` for the same reason the daily run is.
- Afterwards the pinned list fails any pull request that adds a long face, which is the point: that pull request adds its short form and its list entry.

This moves the check, which only reads the card data, into the web's ordinary unit tests, which run on every pull request. The browser test keeps only what needs a real browser, the pixel checks.

## Why
- The premise test, `B15 R1017000 the premise` (`e2e/cypress/component/card-faces.cy.tsx:185-223`), mounts nothing. It works out each face's printed length with `faceModel`, checks that every face over `TEXT_TIER_MAX.xl` (260) has a `shortFormOf`, and pins the list of those faces.
- Component specs run only in the daily super run (its `component` job), or when CI is dispatched with `all` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:39`, `:67`).
- The per-pull-request `apps/web/src/cards/textLimit.test.ts:61-74` checks a line estimate (`FACE_TEXT_LIMIT`), not the 260-character rule. Its header (`:1-4`) leaves that rule to the Cypress spec.
- First slip: `6704528b4` (#974) fixed `component B15` after #967's text for KY's Papaya.
- Second slip: the bot's journal for the open #2067 (`2bf12625d`) records four B15 failures, every one a Stinkyscape face added by #2018. The same journal records a 150-minute build that timed out.

## Proposal
- Move the premise into `apps/web/src/cards/textLimit.test.ts` as a vitest case with the same title, using the same `faceModel`, `shortFormOf` and `TEXT_TIER_MAX`.
- Its pinned list becomes one exported constant that the test and both component specs read. `meditative-faces.cy.tsx:193-216` repeats part of the list.
- The Cypress spec drops its premise test and keeps its pixel tests at 270 px and 170 px.
- Nothing under `.github/` changes, because the web job already runs this file. If `scripts/ci-scope.sh` does not turn the web job on for a card-text-only change, its map gains that path in the same pull request.

## Where it lands
- `apps/web/src/cards/textLimit.test.ts`, with the pinned list beside `SHORT_FORMS` in `apps/web/src/cards/shortText.ts` or in a fixture under `apps/web/src/cards/`.
- `e2e/cypress/component/card-faces.cy.tsx` and `meditative-faces.cy.tsx`.
- `scripts/ci-scope.sh`, only if its map lacks a path the moved test reads.
- R1017000 (`spec/rulings/R1017000.md`) already lists `textLimit.test.ts` in `proven_in`, so it needs no new ruling.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web exec vitest run src/cards/textLimit.test.ts` holds the premise. The PR shows that a face over 260 characters without a short form fails it, and so does a long face missing from the pinned list, each by a local edit that is not committed.
- [ ] Neither component spec keeps a premise test of its own, and all of them read the one shared list.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir e2e test:component` passes `card-faces.cy.tsx` and `meditative-faces.cy.tsx`, or the PR says why it was not run.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh spec check` and `pnpm exec eslint apps/web e2e` are green.

## Size and risks
Small: about 40 lines across four files.
- Build it after #2067 merges, since #2067 adds the Stinkyscape short forms and updates the list. Until then the moved test is red on `main` for the same reason the daily run is.
- Afterwards the pinned list fails any pull request that adds a long face, which is the point: that pull request adds its short form and its list entry.
